title: Strict quotient balancing preserves the diagram projection formula
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, $A/I$ additive torsion, and $P_n=A/I^n$ finite and perfect over $A$ for every $n\geq1$. For a scheme $T$, use its small pro-etale site, the constant ring sheaves $\underline A_T$, $\underline{P_n}_T$, and $A_T=\varprojlim_n\underline{P_n}_T$, with canonical scalar map $\underline A_T\to A_T$ and quotient projections [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. All sites are small in [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $D(A_T)$ and $D(\underline A_T)$ for unbounded derived module categories and $r_T$ for restriction along this scalar map [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$, $\Delta$ be its constant-diagram functor, and $Q_T=(\underline{P_n}_T)_n$ with quotient transitions. On the ringed diagram site [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], define $\mathcal R_T^aL=\Delta L\otimes^L_{\Delta A_T}Q_T$ and $\mathcal R_T^0L_0=\Delta L_0\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}Q_T$. These are actual derived strict towers. For an edge $u:U\to V$ use the canonical coefficient isomorphisms $u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$, $u^{-1}\underline{P_n}_V\cong\underline{P_n}_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], the ordinary ringed operations $L_u^a\dashv R_u^a$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], their strict-diagram operations $\mathscr L_u^a\dashv\mathscr R_u^a$, and the constant-coefficient counterparts $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$. Let $a_u:r_UL_u^a\cong G_ur_V$, $\chi_u:r_VR_u^a\cong R_u^0r_U$, $p_u:r_U\mathscr L_u^a\cong G_ur_V$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^a\cong R_u^{\mathcal T}r_U$ be the normalized flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction].

Let $\rho_L$ and $q_{u,L}$ be the augmentation-preserving strict quotient balancing and pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing].

For every $f:X\to Y$ and ambient $K\in D(A_X)$ let $\pi_f^a:\mathcal R_Y^aR_f^aK\to\mathscr R_f^a\mathcal R_X^aK$ and $\pi_f^0:\mathcal R_Y^0R_f^0r_XK\to R_f^{\mathcal T}\mathcal R_X^0r_XK$ be the diagram-site projection maps, specifically the adjuncts of counit tensored with identity [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. Under the diagonal direct-image identifications, they satisfy
$$(R_f^{\mathcal T}\rho_K)d_{f,\mathcal R_X^aK}\,r_Y(\pi_f^a)=\pi_f^0\mathcal R_Y^0(\chi_{f,K})\rho_{R_f^aK}.$$
The comparisons and equalities hold naturally for arbitrary ambient inputs, without completeness, properness or witnesses; they are equalities in the derived category of strict diagrams, before evaluation or inverse limit.

proof.text: Work on the small diagram sites, not in a category of diagrams in an already localized category. The completed scalar algebra $A_T$ is flat over $\underline A_T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-algebra-flat-quotients], applied with its presentation $S=A_T$ and canonical scalar map. Reindexing $n+1$ by the positive integers leaves this limit unchanged. The completed and finite coefficient identifications $c_S=c_u:u^{-1}A_V\cong A_U$ and $c_{u,n}$, including their compatibility with quotient transitions and projections, are those of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Since $A$ need not be finite, that statement does not cover the constant ring $\underline A$: the identification $c_R:u^{-1}\underline A_V\cong\underline A_U$ is the canonical ring-sheaf isomorphism of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] for the geometric morphism of pro-etale topoi, carrying constant scalar sections to the same scalars; the constant-coefficient operations $G_u\dashv R_u^0$ and $G_u\dashv R_u^{\mathcal T}$ use it. Compatibility with the scalar map, $a_Uc_R=c_Su^{-1}a_V$, is checked after each projection $\pi_{U,n}$, since these jointly determine a map into the limit $A_U$: both $\pi_{U,n}a_Uc_R$ and $c_{u,n}u^{-1}(\pi_{V,n}a_V)$ are ring maps $u^{-1}\underline A_V\to\underline{P_n}_U$ whose adjuncts $\underline A_V\to u_*\underline{P_n}_U$ send a constant section $x$ to the constant section $\bar x$ (by the two constant-section descriptions just cited and $\pi_{V,n}a_V(x)=\bar x$); a map out of the sheafified constant sheaf $\underline A_V$ is determined by the constant sections, so the two adjuncts, hence the two maps, agree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction] with the terminal index category for ordinary modules and with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$ for towers. This gives precisely the normalized comparisons $a,\chi,p,d$ and their adjunct identities. The exact module-diagram equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] places these comparisons in the required derived strict-tower categories.

proof.text:
Fix $f,K$ and suppress $f$ in subscripts. Write $B_T^a=\mathcal R_T^a$, $B_T^0=\mathcal R_T^0$, $L=L_f^a$, $R=R_f^a$, $F=\mathscr L_f^a$, $H=\mathscr R_f^a$, $G=G_f$, and $H_0=R_f^{\mathcal T}$. Write $R_0=R_f^0$ for the ordinary constant-coefficient direct image. For an argument $M$, put $s_M^a:F B_Y^aM\to B_X^a(LM)$ and $s_N^0:G B_Y^0N\to B_X^0(GN)$. Thus $s_M^a=\tau_{f,M}^{-1}$. These are the normalized comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower]. Let $\varepsilon^a:LRK\to K$ and $\varepsilon^0:GR_0r_XK\to r_XK$ be the ordinary counits. By [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] and [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map], $\pi^a$ and $\pi^0$ are respectively adjunct to
$$t^a=B_X^a(\varepsilon^a)s_{RK}^a,\qquad t^0=B_X^0(\varepsilon^0)s_{R_0r_XK}^0.$$
Here the diagonal identifications are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-tower-pushforward-normalization]: its strict counit equation identifies the diagram counit after the constant/direct-image comparison with the diagonal of the ordinary counit. Thus these are the specified projection maps, not maps chosen by their evaluations.

source.place: Second paragraph, the same projection-formula identifications; Stacks 0B56 (sites-cohomology.tex, equation-projection-formula-map), with strict diagonal counit normalization.

proof.text:
The ordinary adjunct identity in [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction], applied to $\varepsilon^a$ whose adjunct is $1_{RK}$, says that $r_X(\varepsilon^a)a_{RK}^{-1}$ has adjunct $\chi_K:r_YRK\to R_0r_XK$. Expanding the inverse Hom bijection, its value is also $\varepsilon^0G(\chi_K)$. Therefore
$$r_X(\varepsilon^a)a_{RK}^{-1}=\varepsilon^0G(\chi_K).$$
This derives the required counit equation from the stated normalization; no compatibility of arbitrarily chosen comparison isomorphisms is being assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph, projection-formula conjugation: ordinary scalar-counit square, obtained from the normalized adjunct identity (Stacks 0FND).

proof.text:
Use [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing] for the arbitrary ambient argument $M=RK$. With $s^a,s^0$ oriented as in Step 2, its pullback equation reads
$$G(\rho_M)p_{B_Y^aM}= (s_{r_YM}^0)^{-1}B_X^0(a_M)\rho_{LM}r_X(s_M^a).$$
Indeed this is its displayed equation for $\tau_{f,M}=(s_M^a)^{-1}$, with the canonical identification $B_X^0G\cong G B_Y^0$ written as $(s^0)^{-1}$. These two identifications hold because the balancing statement's $\tau$ is the pullback/tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on the ringed diagram sites, computed by applying module pullback to K-flat resolutions with flat terms, and on such a representative of $\Delta M$ (and the flat-term tower $Q_Y$) it is the inverse of the termwise map $F(x\otimes q)\mapsto F(x)\otimes F(q)$; [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] says that $s^a$ (its $\tau$ for the coefficients $A_T$, $Q=(\underline{P_n})_n$) is the unique natural isomorphism with exactly this representative component, and likewise $s^0$ for $\underline A_T$. The pulled-back towers are identified with $Q_X$ by the coefficient isomorphisms of Step 1. Multiplying by the indicated inverses gives
$$\rho_{LM}r_X(s_M^a)p_{B_Y^aM}^{-1}=B_X^0(a_M^{-1})s_{r_YM}^0G(\rho_M).$$
All these are morphisms of derived strict towers. The comparison $s^0$ is natural in its argument by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower].

source.place: Second paragraph, strict quotient scalar balancing and pullback/tensor reassociation before taking inverse limits.

proof.text:
Set $\beta=B_Y^0(\chi_K)\rho_{RK}$ and $\gamma=\rho_K$. Naturality of $\rho$ for the ordinary counit, followed by Steps 4 and 3, gives the following calculation in the strict-tower category:
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma\,r_X(t^a)p_{B_Y^aRK}^{-1}
&=B_X^0(r_X\varepsilon^a)\rho_{LRK}r_X(s_{RK}^a)p_{B_Y^aRK}^{-1}\\
&=B_X^0(r_X\varepsilon^a\,a_{RK}^{-1})s_{r_YRK}^0G(\rho_{RK})\\
&=B_X^0(\varepsilon^0)B_X^0(G\chi_K)s_{r_YRK}^0G(\rho_{RK})\\
&=B_X^0(\varepsilon^0)s_{R_0r_XK}^0G(B_Y^0\chi_K)G(\rho_{RK})
=t^0G(\beta).
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is the naturality asserted by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing]. The last line uses naturality of $s^0$ from [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower] at $\chi_K$. The intervening substitutions are exactly the equations established in Steps 4 and 3; only composition and functoriality are used.

source.place: Second paragraph, explicit projection-formula scalar conjugation calculation; agent expansion of the compatibility claimed there.

proof.text:
Apply the strict-diagram adjunct identity of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction] to $t^a:F B_Y^aRK\to B_X^aK$, whose adjunct is $\pi^a$. It identifies $d_{B_X^aK}r_Y(\pi^a)$ as adjunct to $r_X(t^a)p_{B_Y^aRK}^{-1}$. Postcomposing by $H_0(\gamma)$ makes the adjunct equal to $\gamma r_X(t^a)p_{B_Y^aRK}^{-1}$. By Step 5 this is $t^0G(\beta)$. By the Hom-bijection definition of adjunct and its naturality in the source, this last morphism is adjunct to $\pi^0\beta$; $\pi^0$ is adjunct to $t^0$ by Step 2. The Hom bijection is injective, so
$$H_0(\rho_K)d_{B_X^aK}r_Y(\pi^a)=\pi^0 B_Y^0(\chi_K)\rho_{RK},$$
which is precisely the required equation. Postcomposition and precomposition of adjuncts here follow directly from their formulas $t\mapsto H_0(t)\eta$ and $h\mapsto\varepsilon G(h)$, using naturality of $\eta,\varepsilon$.

source.place: Second paragraph, passage from the counit-tensor calculation to equality of projection maps by the normalized adjunction (Stacks 0B56 and 0FND).

proof.text: The isomorphisms $\rho,q$ and their pullback square are natural on arbitrary ambient objects by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing]; the normalized scalar comparisons and adjunct identity are natural derived diagram comparisons by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]. For a map $K\to K'$, naturality of the counits and of $s^a,s^0$ makes $t^a,t^0$ commute with that map, and the natural Hom bijections carry this to the corresponding squares for $\pi^a,\pi^0$. Hence every composite in the equation is natural in $K$. Every equality above was made on the diagram site and then inside its derived category, so it already includes the quotient transitions. The argument used no property of the ambient input beyond being an object of $D(A_X)$, and introduced no properness, completeness, or witness condition.
